candidates.why: Production gate-collapse case study and conclusive recoverability experiments, but the central verifier-strength-to-regret hypothesis is unconfirmed (p=0.23) and the headline rule is partly definitional.
candidates.caveat: The central quantitative claim - that weaker verifiers pick worse changes - is not confirmed: slope CI [-0.234, 0.120], p=0.23, and retail shows no trend at all.

candidates.why: Honest five-month live deployment, but the headline is underperformance vs SPY reframed as containment, and an exposure-matched passive blend beat it on both axes; evolution evidence is two cycles with one learning applied.
candidates.caveat: An exposure-matched 56% SPY/T-bill blend returned +7.5% with -2.5% max drawdown, better on both axes than the live +5.0%/-6.0%.

candidates.why: First drift-stream evaluation of self-evolving agents: fixed backbone, disjoint train/eval, checkpointed evaluation on all groups, mechanistic prompt autopsies - a well-supported negative result the field needed.
candidates.caveat: Streams use a single fixed block order and the plasticity-stability correlation rests on n=12 points (r=-0.72, p=0.008), suggestive rather than conclusive.

candidates.why: Valuable negative-results ledger, but all end-to-end evidence is simulated FP4 arithmetic over ~1.3% of the training horizon with no seeds or error bars; the gap is halved, not closed.
candidates.caveat: The decisive deltas (0.007-0.014 validation loss) are reported without seeds, error bars, or run-to-run variance estimates.

candidates.why: Theory-backed one-line init fix with 5-seed CIs, direct mechanism verification via noise-energy decomposition, cross-family replication, and released code; peak-gain claims honestly deflated.
candidates.caveat: The retuned gap at alpha/r=12 shrinks to +1.33 pts, and most LR-ratio heatmap sweeps are single runs, so cell-level differences should not be over-read.

candidates.why: Orbit theory verified to machine precision is impressive, but practical gains deflate under the paper's own matched-learning-rate controls and all benchmarks are small-scale; durable contribution is diagnostic, not a better optimizer.
candidates.caveat: On ResNet-18 the matched-effective-lr control explains most of the Adam-map effect and about half of Kinetic Muon's +0.17 pp; on the GPT benchmark everything is within seed noise.

candidates.why: Isolates a concrete geometric cause of vocabulary collapse (common-mode offset b-bar) with injection controls, strip-the-well-row experiments, and a dose threshold across 510 snapshots and 14/17 model lineages - causal evidence, not correlation.
candidates.caveat: Several headline numbers rest on single seeds, and the most practically popular recipe (textbook DPO at beta=0.1) does not collapse even at 3x budget.

candidates.why: Commendably validates simulator-guided decisions with real RL runs, but covers only two injected loopholes with rule-based detectors at 0.6B-4B LoRA/GRPO scale, and its baseline is a noise estimator rather than a rival method.
candidates.caveat: The headline baseline ('5 target RL runs') is a measurement-noise estimator, not a competing prediction method; real reward hacking is far more heterogeneous and detector-dependent.

candidates.why: Clean sign law with dose-response linearity and a CI-backed 8-point 9B accuracy effect, but empirical scope is 10-100 steps, math-only, largely one model fork; strong runner-up behind ECHO in a deep area.
candidates.caveat: The headline 9B accuracy result covers only 10 steps from a fork of a single model with 4 seeds (MASK: a single seed), one domain, and one sampler configuration.

candidates.why: Real-world validated systems work: 82 bugs in 2,408 production kernels across 23 libraries, 76 previously unknown, 41 confirmed/fixed upstream, with head-to-head detection counts vs compute-sanitizer and Volta.
candidates.caveat: The tool comparison is evaluated on the set of 82 bugs Racer itself found, which biases the deck; bugs invisible to Racer's refusal semantics are never counted against it.

candidates.why: Statistically careful (30 runs, Welch's t-test) and genuinely novel attack surface, but the effect is 4-16% latency, end-to-end Rowhammer feasibility on modern DIMMs is cited rather than shown, and mitigations are trivial.
candidates.caveat: The paper does not report Rowhammer success rates or time-to-flip for the victim mapping step, so true end-to-end feasibility on modern DDR5 systems is asserted via citations, not demonstrated.

candidates.why: Right controls (real-flip damage checks, gradient-norm control) and honest negatives, but most entries are single runs, the 500-flip headline holds in only 2 of 3 seeds, and the ECC code is idealized rather than simulated.
candidates.caveat: Most table entries are single runs; the headline 500-flip survival sits at a threshold and varies with the training seed - the seed-robust claim is 300 flips.

candidates.why: Strong paired design, public artifacts, and a merged upstream fix, but condition B confounds disclosure with behavioral instructions, the 90/90 verifier flip uses author-written worst-case answers, and no base rate exists; runner-up to a cleaner area peer.
candidates.caveat: Condition B bundles factual disclosures with behavioral instructions, so the headline effects cannot be attributed to disclosure alone; cases were adversarially selected from one system.

candidates.why: Clean mechanistic tracing of the record-over-reality bias with GroupKFold and a random-veto control, but live phone evidence is a 24-task text simulator, failures are injected at 30-40%, and random veto nearly matches EviGate in ALFWorld.
candidates.caveat: The live phone result is not AndroidWorld but a 24-task text simulator, and in ALFWorld random veto reaches 58.2% vs EviGate's 61.2%.

candidates.why: Deterministic OOXML ground truth (no LLM judge), paired exact sign tests with Holm correction, a pre-registered confirmatory experiment, validation on Microsoft's external OCB track, and a 6,462-file prevalence scan - production-reliability evidence of high quality.
candidates.caveat: The headline typing effect sits right at the significance threshold (pHolm = 0.049) and replicates on only 3 of 6 answering models.

candidates.why: Crisp, fully demonstrated numerical diagnosis (target-logit gradient death at the precision cliff) with seeds, error bars, and the two most relevant prior fixes as baselines, in ~30 reproducible lines; scale, not rigor, is the limitation.
candidates.caveat: All evidence comes from tiny algorithmic grokking tasks (width-64 Transformers, modular arithmetic); there is no experiment on any realistic workload.

candidates.why: Airtight solver-certified legality bands with hardware replay and proved faithfulness, but it is one rewrite on one format under one execution model - a compiler-legality lemma rather than a general correctness framework.
candidates.caveat: Scope is one format (MXFP4), one rewrite, one accumulator type; FTZ, wider accumulators, FMA-bearing pipelines, and native block-scaled tensor-core instructions are all outside the certified model.

candidates.why: Disciplined dose-matched, pre-registered methodology with a working validation-gated abstention rule, but the evaluation footprint is small (25-100 queries per dataset), collapse is demonstrated on only 2 of 3 models, and the sealed test was never run.
candidates.caveat: Evaluation scale is small - 25 disjoint queries per domain in-domain and 100 queries / 2,000 documents per held-out dataset - so absolute NDCG is not headlined.

candidates.why: Every claim adjudicated by causal splicing interventions with position-code controls across 11 models and 14 relational tasks, code and 85-page SI released - a real mechanistic account of in-context relational binding.
candidates.caveat: Task scale is minimal: two-edge graphs with single-token, position-aligned entity names, so the boundary of the claimed organization is unknown; the ~10B emergence claim is correlational.

candidates.why: Methodologically excellent (exact permutation negative controls, pre-registered thresholds), but the reader-writer pairing is statistically real yet functionally near-interchangeable (millinat effects) and the cheap weights-only diagnostic fails on gated SwiGLU architectures.
candidates.caveat: The equal-disturbance loss effect is only 4-9 millinats, and after writer-permutation breaks a different assignment reaches the control loss - the pairing is functionally near-interchangeable.

candidates.why: High-rigor pre-registered probing study with an important methodological warning (failed probe does not mean absent information), but only two ~1.5B models on a narrow two-form task family with acknowledged post-hoc concessions.
candidates.caveat: Only two small models, computation studies on Ouro alone, and P1 probing requires feeding in the gold answer, which limits ecological validity.

candidates.why: Config-matched 512-GPU measurements with per-component ablations and replayed real selections: 2.07x over Megatron-LM at 1M-token context, with mathematical equivalence argument and honestly stated heuristics.
candidates.caveat: The paper never shows a training-loss curve comparing HyScale vs Megatron-LM over a long run - timing experiments average steps 4-10 - and no code release is mentioned.

candidates.why: Unusually good matched-compute ablation design isolating the scoring signal from the budget mechanism, but no seed variance on the +0.60 8B headline and SFT-only scope on a single model family.
candidates.caveat: No seed variance or repeated runs are reported, so the headline +0.60 overall improvement at 8B on LongBench-Pro could plausibly be noise.

candidates.why: Well-modeled architecture study with open simulator, but entirely simulation-based with no RTL or silicon validation, and the 2.23x headline comes from dated MHA-based GPT3-175B while the modern GQA case averages 1.29-1.61x.
candidates.caveat: All results are simulation-only - no silicon, FPGA, or even RTL-on-emulator validation of the TSV direct-forwarding path or the MC timing handshake.

candidates.why: Unusually honest, detailed open-weights release worth knowing, but as evidence it is weakest in class: all baselines self-run under its own protocol, in-house German benchmarks, and real weak rows (closed-book last of 14 models).
candidates.caveat: All baseline numbers are self-run under their own protocol, and several German benchmark versions plus five in-house Industry RAG proxies are not publicly available.

candidates.why: Competitive open agentic model with a concrete reward-hacking mitigation section, but no component-level ablations anywhere, self-reported baselines with anomalous entries, and clear regressions on the hardest terminal benchmarks.
candidates.caveat: The headline 1.93x efficiency gain is reported only as an aggregate against one Qwen3-style baseline with no decomposition of which components contribute.

candidates.why: Interesting learned-orchestration framing with real teacher ablations, but the 'matches or surpasses on all twelve benchmarks' headline is contradicted by its own table, key toggles are within run-to-run noise, and science showcases are n=1.
candidates.caveat: Table 1 shows Sage-A1.5 below A1 on GAIA (95.1 vs 96.0), HiPhO and MatTools; the +1.1 orchestration gain on BrowseComp is within plausible run-to-run noise.
